standard_prerequisites.name: Numerical types and their Picard group
standard_prerequisites.statement: A numerical type is a collection of integers n, m of subscript i, a of subscript i j, w of subscript i and g of subscript i satisfying the symmetry and recurrence conditions of the chapter, and its Picard group is defined as the cokernel of the matrix of the rational quotients a of subscript i j over w of subscript i; the author's own notation is retained inside the counted statement and proof.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma compares that presentation of the Picard group with the cokernel of the plain intersection matrix, and the comparison is the input for the rank computation and the embedding statements that follow in the same section.

core_obligations: Recall the presentation of the Picard group as the cokernel of the matrix whose entries are the intersection numbers divided by the weights, so that its row module is the free module on the vertices (source line 1150).

Build the commutative diagram of two short exact rows: the upper row presents the cokernel of the intersection matrix, the lower row presents the Picard group, the left vertical map is the identity and the right vertical map is the diagonal matrix of the weights (source lines 1151-1164).

Check that the diagram commutes, which is exactly the identity expressing the divided matrix as the intersection matrix composed with the inverse of the diagonal matrix of the weights, and then apply the snake lemma to the resulting comparison to conclude the embedding of the Picard group into the cokernel of the intersection matrix (source lines 1165-1166).

proof_roadmap.step: Recall that the Picard group is the cokernel of the divided intersection matrix.
Write down the two exact rows with the identity on the left and the diagonal weight matrix on the right.
Apply the snake lemma to obtain the inclusion of the Picard group in the cokernel of the intersection matrix.
